scope: High-value native C/C++ memory, lifetime, exception, container, and concurrency coverage. This crosswalk records rule assets, not runtime enablement.

priorities.gap: No local syntactic rule: reliable coverage requires lifetime/data-flow analysis.
Pack rules cover same-function allocation/deallocation mismatches; double free and cross-function ownership remain CodeQL work.
No local rule currently models allocation APIs and failure contracts across calls.
No equivalent local syntactic or imported analyzer mapping.
No local syntactic rule can calculate type size and alignment safely.
Pack rule covers smart pointers built from another owner's get(); raw pointers stored earlier remain CodeQL work.
No local syntactic rule can resolve effective alignment and allocation overloads.
The former local array-new/scalar-delete rule now maps to MEM51-CPP, which owns that case on the official page; deleting arrays through a pointer of another static type requires type resolution.
Pack rule covers views, pointers, and iterators returned into destroyed locals; general lifetime analysis remains CodeQL work.
The former local string_view rule now maps to EXP54-CPP because it concerns object lifetime; invalidation by string operations requires data-flow analysis.
No local rule added because a syntax-only subscript match is too noisy.
No local syntactic or analyzer mapping equivalent; mutation-aware lifetime analysis is required.
No local pattern or imported mapping establishes exception guarantees.
No local syntactic equivalent; path-sensitive resource modeling is required.

priorities.weakness: mutex destroyed or leaves scope while locked
priorities.gap: Pack rule covers the direct POSIX lock/destroy sequence only.
Pack rule covers a direct manual lock followed by throw; interprocedural exceptional exits require deeper analysis.
Pack rule does not prove that a surrounding loop re-tests the predicate.
Pack rule covers a same-function relock of a declared non-recursive mutex only.

known_gaps: This bundle does not enable or license the CodeQL CLI; the generic C/C++ workflow must supply an approved CLI and the lock-file dependencies.
Semgrep/OpenGrep rules referenced here live in the rules/sei-cert pack, which pins and executes both engines; its mappings, not this crosswalk, are authoritative for rule-pack coverage status.
CodeChecker files are mappings only; they do not install or enable clang-tidy, Clang Static Analyzer, or Cppcheck checkers.
MISRA and AUTOSAR rule prose, examples, and commercial checker content are intentionally excluded because redistribution and derivative rights were not established.
A mapped CERT identifier is evidence of a crosswalk, not evidence that a checker is installed, enabled, or complete.
